input.quote: 7.2 Before engaging another provider, Customer must disclose and match for Vendor any more favourable commercial offer it receives.
input.rationale: Section 7.2 imposes a right of first refusal on Customer: we may not engage another provider unless we first disclose a competing offer to Vendor and match it. That is a de facto exclusivity restriction binding our party, and it fails the fallback in every material respect — it is not limited to a defined service category, has no 12-month sunset, and has no automatic termination on Vendor's failure to meet service levels or delivery dates. It effectively operates for the full three-year term (Section 8.1) with no performance-based exit, which is walk-away territory. It also directly contradicts Section 12.3, in which Vendor acknowledges Customer has made no exclusivity commitment. The redline restores the preferred position (no exclusivity or first-refusal gate on our sourcing freedom) with the smallest edit to Section 7.2; the pricing-disclosure/MFN dimension of the same sentence is left to the MFN rule and is not separately flagged here. The Customer non-compete in the second Section 12.4 and the minimum volume commitment in Section 2.1 are addressed under their own rules.

proposal.summary: Remove the de facto exclusivity / right-of-first-refusal gate in Section 7.2 on Customer engaging another provider.
proposal.comment: [Playbook] We cannot accept a right of first refusal that requires us to disclose and match a competing offer before we may engage another provider; our playbook position is that we retain full freedom to source from other suppliers, and this also conflicts with Section 12.3. If some form of restriction is essential, we could look at exclusivity limited to a single defined service category for no more than twelve months, ending automatically if Vendor misses a service level or delivery date.

ops.oldText: 7.2 Before engaging another provider, Customer must disclose and match for Vendor any more favourable commercial offer it receives.
ops.newText: 7.2 Customer may engage any other provider at any time and is not required to notify Vendor of, disclose, or match any competing or more favourable commercial offer it receives as a condition of doing so.
